welding raised the transition temperature because it created a large grain size
Worked molybdenum - 0.5-percent-titanium specimens show small carbide inclusions (fig. 5(h)) .
Worked molybdenum specimens show very large carbide particles (fig. 5(c)).
Upon recrystallization the carbides redissolve, and upon slow cooling large carbide precipitates appear at the grain boundaries, as shown in figure 5(1).

welded specimens mainly show fine precipitates in the matrix (fig. 5( j), p. 10). This structure is the result of the redissolving of the precipitate upon fusion. The more rapid rate of cooling during the welding process allowed carbides to precipitate within the grains.
At the extreme left is a portion of the fused zone of the weld where the total cross section of the metal is comprised of as few as 2 to 5 grains.
At the extreme left is a portion of the fused zone of the weld where the total cross section of the metal is comprised of as few as 2 to 5 grains.
sizes essentially the same as those obtained in the fusion zones of welds (figs. 5(a), (d), (f), and (i)); that is, the specimens have approximately 2 to 5 grains across the 0.040-inch thickness.
Both materials, when annealed at 2000° or 2400° F to give recrystallized structures, gave fine grain structures (about 3500 grains/ sq mm).
Both materials, when annealed at 2000° or 2400° F to give recrystallized structures, gave fine grain structures (about 3500 grains/ sq mm).
The grain size decreases toward the right until the area containing fibrous, unaffected base metal is finally reached.
Farther to the right is the heat- affected zone, where recrystallization has occurred.

Metallographic study revealed fewer grain-boundary precipitates in the welded specimens than in those annealed at 3500' F, probably because the faster cooling rate of the welded metal had left less time for precipitation to OCCUT.

conflicts.description: Carbon content of as-received Mo-0.5Ti: vendor analysis reports 220 ppm, commercial analysis reports 310 ppm.

evidence.quote: The vendor's analysis of the as-received molybdenum - 0.5-percent-titanium alloy showed 220 parts carbon per million, while the commercial analysis given in table I11 indicates 310 parts carbon per million.
